_comment: The path contract, enforced by `devkit lint-paths`.
The finding behind it: `~` is a shell construct. It expands only in a
shell, unquoted, at word start. It does NOT expand in a markdown link target,
a JSON or TOML value, a .desktop Exec= line, a symlink target, cron's command
position, or a quoted shell string — "~/x" stays literal even in bash.
So: ${HOME} is the only home-anchored token in kit source, rendered per context
at install. A literal /home/<user> never ships. `~/` is allowed only in prose,
where a human reads it and no program resolves it.
core/ is linted: it is kit source after export. Vendored upstream docs under core/kb/offline-reference are excluded — they are third-party text the kit copies verbatim and cannot edit.
The vendored minified diff2html bundle is excluded: a `~` in minified JS is an operator, not a path, and the file is third-party.

machine_consumed._comment: Extensions whose content a program parses. ~/ and literal home paths are errors here.

prose._comment: Human-read files. ~/ is fine in prose; a literal home path is still an error because it names one machine.

_comment: Shell and Python. ~/ is an error inside quotes and in any non-word-start
position; $HOME and ${HOME} are correct. A literal home path is always an error.
The ${HOME:-/home/leanon} fallback pattern in the sync scripts is the
specific case that motivated this: the fallback bakes in one machine's username.

rules.message: literal home path into a harness directory names one machine
rules.fix: use ${HOME} (kit source) or $HOME (shell), never a hardcoded home
rules._comment: Anchored to a harness dotdir on purpose. A bare /home/<x>/ also matches container paths (/enonic-xp/home/, a Dockerfile's /home/builder) which are correct as written and not this machine's home.

rules.message: literal macOS home path names one machine
~ does not expand in a parsed value; it is read as a relative path
rules.fix: use ${HOME}, which install.py renders for this context

rules.message: ~ in a link target renders as the relative path ./~/...
rules.fix: link a repo-relative path, or write the ~/ form as inline code instead

rules.message: a HOME fallback bakes one machine's home into every other machine
rules.fix: require HOME, or fail with a message naming it

rules.message: ~ inside quotes stays literal even in bash
rules._comment: Shell only. In Python a "~/..." literal is usually prose in a help string, or is about to go through expanduser(), neither of which is the bug this rule describes.

allow._comment: An exemption is a claim that a human reads that line and no program resolves it. tests/test_devkit.py holds deliberate positive fixtures: a test proving a rule fires must contain the string the rule matches. docs/paths.md, install.md and troubleshooting.md document the rules themselves, quoting example paths and error messages. Prose files already have inline code stripped before matching, so these cover only fenced blocks and running text.

shell._comment: Shell scripts specifically. Quoting defeats ~ expansion here and nowhere else.
